concerns.message: The design says the ledger pre-check "on the same synchronous tick guarantees" that `purchase` succeeds after intel delivers. That only holds for one request per player per tick. The room queues requests between world ticks, and the journal shows one Buy button per missing type. Take a slice player who lacks both types and has 25–49 gold (for example 40 after losing a duel from 50) and sends two requests of different types in one tick. Both pass the pre-check. `stepIntel` delivers both, because they are different (player, type) entries, each answered `rumor`. The first `purchase` leaves less than 25 gold, so the second is refused with `insufficient-gold`.
concerns.consequence: The "fault" guard fires in normal play, not only under injection. By then intel's state already holds the withheld rumor as an active journal entry: `fresh()` skips that target for later leads, entry numbers skip one, and later `rumor-stale` or `rumor-resolved` messages name an entry the client never saw. The ledger also keeps an `insufficient-gold` refusal under that client id (economy.ts:170-172), so every retry becomes a replayed refusal. The fix must be settled before anyone writes the purchase queue: either the pre-check reserves gold across a player's requests in the tick, or the room takes at most one purchase per player per tick and leaves the rest queued.

concerns.message: "A retried id that was refused is decided again, because nothing was kept" is only true for refusals from the room's pre-check. `stepIntel` adds every accepted request id to `state.requestIds` whatever the answer: `none` before control start, `covered`, `capped`, `none` (step.ts:535). Retrying a refused id under the same `<playerId>:<clientRequestId>` returns `duplicate` forever.
concerns.consequence: A test or doc written to the stated rule fails, or the UI shows a permanent refusal for a retry (for example `capped` now, available after the next snapshot). Either document that intel's refusals are final, or add an attempt counter to the intel id and rely on the room's own record for idempotency.

concerns.message: The pre-check only asks the ledger (in play, not in a duel, not disconnected, 25 gold or more). Any request that passes reaches `stepIntel`, which keeps every id forever and re-sorts the whole `requestIds` array on each tick that has a request. A client moored with 25 gold can send an unlimited stream of fresh ids for a type with no lead, or a covered one. They are never charged and are all kept. The ledger caps kept refusals at 16 per player exactly so that "a client cannot grow the state without limit". The `docs/objectives.md` Rumor flow also asks for an availability check first.
concerns.consequence: Intel state grows without bound and each tick with a request pays for a larger sort, so a hostile or buggy client causes tick overruns across a 35-minute match. Add a `targetedRumorAvailability` check (`rumor` or `sighting` required) to the pre-check, and a per-session rate cap like `ruinRate`. Only the rare same-tick race then reaches intel as a refusal.

concerns.message: Retry order: if the room runs the ledger pre-check before looking up its record of bought ids, a retry of a bought id after the player has spent gold below 25 (or during a duel) is refused with `insufficient-gold` or `player-in-duel` instead of being replayed.
concerns.consequence: This breaks acceptance 3's "a retry … is replayed" whenever the retry arrives after gold changed, and the client may show a refusal for a rumor it already has. Look up the record, or the ledger's `requests`, first, as `purchase` itself does (economy.ts:147).

concerns.message: The design says "intel's state keeps only active island and sector leads", and its delivery list is rumors, sightings, stale notices and no-lead. In fact `IntelPlayerState.journal` keeps every rumor with status active, stale or resolved, and the step emits `rumor-resolved` when the player gets the type. The journal-record design has no resolved state.
concerns.consequence: If `rumor-resolved` is not mapped and logged, a rumor for a type the player has just collected (or stolen) stays under "current rumors" in the journal and after a reconnect. Map `rumor-resolved` and give the log entries a resolved status.

concerns.message: Replacement links are matched by type. When a player loses type T on the same tick that their T rumor goes stale, `gatherLeads` keeps one free trigger, and `compareFree` chooses `fresh` over `replacement`. The only lead that arrives has reason `fresh`, so the stale entry never gets a replacement with reason `replacement`. A deferred sighting can also carry reason `fresh` for a type whose rumor went stale earlier.
concerns.consequence: Stale entries show no replacement, or the UI's link rule and its unit tests disagree with what the room sends. Link a stale entry to the next lead of the same type whatever its reason, and test that case.

concerns.message: The fault guard ("withhold the lead, log a fault, and a test covers it") needs a test-only seam that makes `purchase` fail after the pre-check. The coverage table forbids `unreachable` rows. Withholding also leaves intel's state out of step with what the client saw, and that step cannot be rolled back because it already produced other players' messages.
concerns.consequence: Adding a fault-injection hook and its coverage-table row takes time out of a three-hour budget, and the fault path leaves a corrupted journal. Once concern 1 is fixed the guard is a true invariant, so assert it (throw, which aborts the match per §12) and test it through the existing `testHooks`.

concerns.message: `docs/objectives.md` is owned, and its "Rumor flow" paragraph gives the old order: availability, then `purchase`, then deliver, with deliver on `ok && !replayed`. The plan only says to document the new order in `docs/architecture.md`.
concerns.consequence: The two docs contradict each other about a money path. `economy-online`'s shop will read `objectives.md` and could follow the old charge-first order. Update that paragraph too.

structured_output.simpler_alternative: Use the ledger's own pure `purchase` as the pre-check. Call `purchase(this.ledger, {requestId: clientId, playerId, item: "rumor", tick})` on the current ledger state and hold the returned state without committing it. That call already handles the replay lookup first (a bought id comes back `replayed`, answered from the room's record without touching intel), the disconnected, in-duel and insufficient-gold refusals with the ledger's exact reasons, and per-player ids. Also require `targetedRumorAvailability` ∈ {rumor, sighting}. Chain one player's requests in a tick through the tentative ledger state, or take one per player per tick. Pass only the survivors to `stepIntel` under the namespaced id, then commit each held ledger state only when intel answers `rumor` or `sighting`, and throw it away otherwise, so refusals are never kept and are decided again. There is no duplicated pre-check logic, and no gap between the check and the charge. The multi-request and retry-order bugs disappear.
structured_output.cheap_experiment: Write a 20-line vitest against the pure modules on `main`, with no room. Build a slice ledger and intel state with one player who lacks both types and has 40 gold (lower `startingGold`), past control start. Run the planned sequence (ledger-style pre-check for each request, then one `stepIntel` with two requests of different types, then `purchase` for each delivered outcome) and assert that the second `purchase` returns `insufficient-gold` while intel has already added two active journal rumors. Then send a request that came back `none` or `covered` to `stepIntel` again under the same id and assert that it now returns `duplicate`. If both assertions hold, the multi-request fix and the retry wording have to be settled before the worker starts.
